summary.headline: Aether Q2 FY27: CRAMS and CEM contribute over 65% of sales; first semiconductor commercial shipments began, Magnum CEM contract starts Q4 FY27.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a solid quarter, with CRAMS and CEM together contributing over 65% of sales and oil and gas at 33%. The company shipped a new set of oilfield chemicals to Baker Hughes in Q2 and made its first commercial semiconductor shipments from existing facilities, with volumes still modest. A new CEM contract with a global agrochemical innovator was signed, with production at Magnum starting Q4 FY27 at 200-250 tons per year. Management reiterated capex of INR350-370 crores for FY27 and flagged inventory days rising to 172 from 151 in March, with working capital at around 165 days in the Q&A.

financial_highlights.metric: Oil and gas share of sales
Baker Hughes revenue in quarter (per analyst, Bhavika)
financial_highlights.value: around INR87 crores from Site and pilot plant

financial_highlights.change: approximately INR400 crores expected to capitalise by FY27 end, mainly Site 5

segments.name: CRAMS and CEM
segments.commentary: Together over 65% of sales, driven by ramp-up of major CEM contracts and new CRAMS projects. More than 65 CRAMS projects in R&D and pilot plant; 16 new customers added in H1.

segments.name: Oil and gas (Baker Hughes)
segments.commentary: Oil and gas is 33% of sales. New oilfield chemicals shipped to Baker Hughes in Q2 from Strata (Site 4); management sees total Baker opportunity at INR750-800 crores, with a target of more than USD100 million (about INR1,000 crores) of business.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: First commercial shipments from existing facilities, volumes modest but growing month on month. Magnum semiconductor block on track for commercial production from Q4 FY27; INR300-400 crores top line targeted at maturity, around 2029.

segments.name: Pharma and agrochemical (LSM/CEM)
segments.commentary: Share has been declining as plants were re-equipped for CEM and focus shifted to material sciences and oil and gas. First LSM pharma blocks at Magnum are ramping step by step; new agrochemical CEM contract starts Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management said EBITDA margins will exceed the 30% that it has been guiding, but it is staying conservative given war and pricing risks.
FY27 capex expected at INR350-370 crores; civil work is largely done on eight blocks, so equipment spend will be phased.
About INR400 crores of CWIP (mainly Site 5) expected to be capitalised by end of FY27.
Working capital cycle expected to improve quarter on quarter; inventory levels expected to fall once CEM production is full-fledged.
Target of 25% of revenue from oil and gas, material science, pharma, agro and other sectors; oil and gas and material science to grow faster than pharma and agro.
Two LSM products per year minimum planned for launch; 12 to 15 LSM projects in R&D.
capex_capacity: Magnum site: 16 production blocks on 31 acres; line of sight on 14 blocks, 2 earmarked for LSM and 12 for CEM, to be commercialised over the next 2-3 years.
Agrochemical CEM contract: start at 200-250 tons per year in Q4 FY27 from Magnum block 4, with a path to around 600 tons per year; first supply from Jan-Feb.
Material science contract with a European multinational: 1 plant of 1,000 tons per year at Site 5, extending 1-2 products to 5-6.
Strata (Site 4): Baker Hughes new products run on one modified production line with no new block needed; asset turns expected at 3-3.5x at maturity.
Dow silicones: multiyear research programme; immediate goal is a pilot unit before a commercial multi-kiloton plant.
R&D operations moving from 24/6 to 24/7, to be completed over about a month.
demand_pricing: Baker Hughes: the new products address a market of USD2-2.5 billion, per management; the existing pour point depressant opportunity was INR400 crores, with the new products a further INR400 crores.

Semiconductor molecules: average market price USD45-50 per kg; target 300-400 tons of sales by FY29; products are building blocks for silane coupling agents and copper clad laminates for high-speed PCBs.
Agrochemical CEM: pricing confidential; the molecule is a patented launch molecule from an innovator, with 50 tons initially and rising to 600 tons.
Contract manufacturing passes through raw material price increases, per management, which reduces inventory-price risk on CEM contracts.
Management declines HF, F2 and H2S chemistries and says it says no to inquiries frequently, prioritising cash flow and IRR.

qa_highlights.question: How has Aether codified knowledge to reduce key-person dependency in R&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Desai cited a flat structure with 12 group leaders (8 research, 4 chemical engineering, plus chemists) who have been with the company for 10+ years, with separate labs and access controls; he said the work is a team effort.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross and EBITDA margins rise as complexity increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Faiz Nagariya said gross margins will improve with the shift to CEM and CRAMS, and EBITDA margins will exceed the 30% guidance, but management is staying conservative for war and pricing risks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market and revenue potential of the new Baker Hughes products?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan Desai put the market at USD2-2.5 billion and set a target of more than USD100 million (about INR1,000 crores) of business with Baker Hughes in the near future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Baker Hughes opportunity after the new products, and what asset turns can Strata deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: Kushal Doshi said the total Baker opportunity is INR750-800 crores, covered by original Strata capex, with asset turns of 3-3.5x at maturity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for FY27 and FY28 given Magnum and R&D expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Faiz Nagariya guided FY27 capex to INR350-370 crores, as civil work is largely done and equipment will be ordered as required.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory building up and what is its composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Faiz Nagariya said the build-up is due to new sites (Milliken and Magnum) and far-east sourced raw materials with long lead times; inventory is not tracked separately for CEM and LSM, and reduction is targeted.

risks_watch: Inventory days and working capital cycle: 165 days (up 3 from March), with management declining to give a forward target.
Magnum site ramp-up: first agrochemical CEM production and semiconductor production both start in Q4 FY27; the timeline is management's and has not yet been verified.

Pending announcements: oil and gas major plant dedication, multinational material science collaboration (2 plants, plus 2 in reserve), and a European multinational expansion (5 of 16 blocks in a best case); none has been confirmed yet.
Interest rate and capitalised interest were not disclosed; management offered to follow up separately.
Pharma and agro share of sales is declining; the LSM ramp-up at Magnum is being taken step by step.
Management described the macro environment as volatile, citing war situations and pricing effects.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on pipeline, customer wins and Magnum expansion, with several forward claims (Magnum ahead of schedule, large best-case partnerships) left unquantified. More cautious on margins, inventory and capex, and declined to disclose interest rates, customer run rates and TAM.
key_quotes: Our CRAMS and CEM businesses continues to lead. Together, they now contribute over 65% of our sales.
We have started our first commercial shipments to semiconductor customers from our existing production facilities.
Pricing is confidential, needless to say, but we plan to start at 200 to 250 tons per year in Q4 FY 2027 with a projected path of around 600 tons per year over time.
We don't give any future guidance on growth over the next 2 or 3 years.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth % guided; management guides EBITDA margin above 30%, FY27 capex INR350-370 cr, and a new agrochemical CEM contract starting Q4 FY27 at 200-250 t/yr with a Baker Hughes opportunity of INR750-800 cr, backed by specific contracts and blocks but with no revenue number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says EBITDA margins will exceed the 30% guidance and gross margins improve with the shift to CEM and CRAMS, though it is staying conservative on war and pricing risks.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Magnum agrochemical CEM block 4 starts at 200-250 t/yr in Q4 FY27 with a path to about 600 t/yr, and Magnum semiconductor block moves to commercial production in Q4 FY27; about INR400 crore of CWIP (mainly Site 5) is expected to capitalise by FY27 end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: New CEM contract ramps from 50 t initially to 200-250 t/yr from Q4 FY27, 16 new CRAMS customers were added in H1, and first semiconductor shipments are growing month on month, though no revenue growth % was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is held at INR350-370 crore with civil work largely done on eight blocks, and pending multinational material-science and oil and gas plant announcements are unconfirmed, so a new capex round depends on those deals closing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says EBITDA margins will exceed 30% but is staying conservative, and the Baker Hughes opportunity of INR750-800 crore plus a USD100 million (about INR1,000 crore) target is not yet in numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital is about 165 days (up 3 days from March), inventory days rose to 172 from 151, management gave no forward target, and war and pricing risks are flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two LSM products a year minimum are planned, 12-15 LSM projects are in R&D, and semiconductor and agrochemical CEM molecules start production from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Baker Hughes oilfield chemicals ramp
rows.why: New products shipped in Q2 from Strata (Site 4) on an existing line, with about INR87 crore of Baker revenue in the quarter and a total opportunity of INR750-800 crore against a USD2-2.5 billion market.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital reduction
rows.why: Working capital cycle is around 165 days, and management expects a quarter-on-quarter improvement once CEM production is full-fledged, but it declined to give a forward target.

rows.label: European multinational material-science plant at Site 5
rows.why: A 1,000 t/yr plant is planned for a European multinational, but the deal is unconfirmed, with 2 plants plus 2 in reserve pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline, Baker Hughes wins, and Magnum timing, but cautious on margins, inventory and rates, while analysts pressed on inventory days, working capital, CWIP and the unconfirmed partnerships.
